query: In an on-site fishpond enforcement scenario, low-concentration mixed residues of banned aquaculture drugs must be detected in water samples. Design a practical sample-preprocessing and Raman/SERS detection workflow for field use. Explain how detection sensitivity and accuracy can be maintained under high background fluorescence and complex matrix conditions, and propose feasible optimization measures.

For Raman/SERS detection of low-concentration mixed banned aquaculture-drug residues in fishpond water, propose a complete spectral data-analysis and algorithmic workflow. The answer should include preprocessing, feature extraction, multi-component identification, quantitative modeling, and innovative suggestions for improving discrimination among structurally similar drugs.

A portable Raman/SERS system is planned for fishpond on-site enforcement. Provide a system-integration plan covering the light source, detector, sample-processing module, algorithm runtime environment, and data-output interface. The design should focus on portability, cost control, power supply, environmental robustness, and practical usability in field inspection.

For Raman/SERS-based detection of banned aquaculture drugs in fishpond water, propose two to three concrete innovation directions, for example in SERS substrate design, spectral enhancement, algorithmic modeling, or anti-interference design. Explain how these improvements would enhance analytical performance and enforcement operability.

If fishpond water samples contain strong fluorescence background or high turbidity interference, propose a robust detection and algorithmic strategy to ensure that low-concentration mixed banned aquaculture-drug residues can still be reliably detected. Explain how this robustness should be implemented and validated at the system level.
